transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, it's probably not a huge deal compared to what you usually see, but... I guess the main reason I made the appointment is that I just get pulled off track so easily? 

Like, I'll be trying to finish up a dashboard for a project, and just one little Slack ping, or even a song lyric playing in the background, or a random idea for a totally different project pops into my head... and suddenly I’ve just completely lost the thread of what I was supposed to be doing. I feel really guilty about it because I always try to do my best and be reliable, you know? Um, is that... does that make sense for why someone would come see you?

Thinking back, did you notice these kinds of concentration and distractibility difficulties when you were a kid in school, or is this something that's really only become a problem for you as an adult?

Um, yeah, I think it's always been there, if I'm being honest. Like, even back in elementary school... I hope it's okay to bring up stuff from that long ago? 

But, um, I was a really good kid, I promise, I always tried my best! It's just... my teachers used to write comments on my report cards sometimes. They'd say I was, like, rushing through my worksheets a bit too fast, or maybe losing track of the directions. And I guess I had a habit of talking over my classmates during group work? I always felt so terrible when they pointed that out, I really didn't mean to be disruptive or rude, I think I just got a little too eager to participate. 

And at home, my parents were so sweet, they actually used to sit right beside me while I did my homework. Not because I wasn't smart enough to do it, but just because if they didn't, I would kind of... wander off, or start a totally different activity before actually finishing the assignment. So I guess it has been happening for a while. Um, I hope that answers your question? Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?

Besides the distractibility, do you also notice things like feeling physically restless, having trouble sitting still, or feeling like you need to be constantly moving or talking, even now as an adult?

Um, yeah, I guess I do still get a little fidgety sometimes? I hope that doesn't make me sound immature, since I'm in college now. I really do try my best to be polite and professional, especially during, like, long Zoom lectures or if I'm supposed to be studying quietly in the library. 

But sometimes, if I have to sit still for a really long time, I just start getting this... I don't know, this kind of uncomfortable pressure? Like my body is just telling me I need to get up and pace around the room, or at least be doing something with my hands, like twirling a pen or something. I try really hard not to let anyone see it because I don't want to be a distraction to anyone else. Does that make sense? I hope that's not too weird of a thing to say.
Do you find that, even now, you often interrupt conversations, blurt out answers or comments before someone finishes speaking, or have difficulty waiting your turn in line or during discussions?

Um, I guess... maybe a little bit? I really, really try not to, because I know how rude it is to interrupt people, and I always want to be respectful of everyone's time and thoughts. But sometimes... especially when we're doing group projects and, like, brainstorming? 

I just get so excited about what we're working on. And I'll accidentally just... blurt out an idea, or I'll jump into the shared Figma board and start adding things before my partner has even finished explaining their thought. I always feel awful about it right after, because I can tell I probably came off as really pushy or bossy, and I promise I don't mean to be! I just get so caught up in the energy of the project. I always apologize right away when I realize I've done it. Is that... is that the kind of thing you mean? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible group member.

Would you say these difficulties with focus, restlessness, or impulsivity have actually caused real problems for you—like affecting your grades, relationships, or job performance—across different areas of your life, or are they more just occasional annoyances that don't really get in the way?

Um... I guess they do get in the way a little bit? I really hate admitting this, because I always want to be someone people can depend on, and I really do try my best. It's not like everything is a disaster, I promise! 

But... well, I do some small freelance design stuff on the side, and... I've actually lost a couple of those small contracts recently. And I ended up missing out on a portfolio competition, too. It definitely wasn't because I didn't care, it's just... I guess people felt like they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly on all the final details. 

And, um, I think it’s even made some of my friends and classmates a little hesitant to collaborate with me on things? They always tell me they really like my ideas, which is so nice of them, but I know they worry about my follow-through. It makes me feel terrible, I never want to be a burden or let anyone down when we work together. Um, does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of example you were asking for, and I really hope it doesn't make me sound too irresponsible.

Would you say that your restlessness and impulsivity—separate from the distractibility—have also caused noticeable problems in more than one area of your life, like both in your coursework and in your personal relationships, or do they mostly show up in just one setting?

Um, I mean... I don't really think the restlessness or, like, the blurting things out causes any major problems? I hope not, anyway. I really try to keep all of that under control so it doesn't bother anyone. 

I guess... I mean, mostly it's just me feeling a little antsy during long classes, or maybe getting a bit too eager during group work, like I mentioned before. But I don't think it's ruining my relationships or anything like that. My friends are really understanding, and I always try to make up for it if I accidentally interrupt someone. I really do want to be a good friend and a good student. 

So, I don't know... I wouldn't say it's causing noticeable problems everywhere, you know? Just maybe some small, embarrassing moments here and there. I hope that's an okay answer? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it actually is.

You mentioned losing freelance contracts and friends being hesitant to collaborate—does the distractibility itself, separate from the restlessness or blurting out, also cause problems in your coursework or classes, not just the freelance work?

Um... I guess maybe? I really don't want to sound like I'm making excuses for my grades or anything, because I know I need to just try harder and be more disciplined. 

But... yeah, I suppose the getting distracted part does make classes a little tough sometimes? Like, I'll be sitting in a lecture, and I really, truly want to pay attention to the professor—I always sit near the front so I can focus better—but then I'll just sort of drift off, or start thinking about a design idea, and suddenly I've missed, like, ten minutes of notes. 

And then when I'm trying to do my reading or homework, it just... it takes me so much longer than everyone else because I keep losing my place or getting sidetracked by something else on my laptop. I always feel so guilty about it, like I'm just being lazy, even though I'm trying really hard. It definitely makes keeping my grades up a lot more stressful than it probably should be. 

Is that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm explaining this right. I just really want to be a good student, you know?

Um... oh, wait, did you mean... I'm sorry, I think I might have confused things earlier. I really didn't mean to! 

When I was talking about losing those small freelance contracts and missing out on that portfolio competition... and, um, my friends and classmates being hesitant to collaborate with me... I think that was actually more because of the restlessness and impulsivity? Like, not just the distractibility. 

I really hate bringing it up again because I don't want you to think I'm completely unreliable or anything. I really do try to be a good partner on projects! But... yeah, I think jumping into things too fast without thinking, or getting impatient and rushing the final details because I just can't sit still long enough to polish them... that's what made people feel like they couldn't rely on me to follow through cleanly. Even though they tell me they like my ideas, which is always so sweet of them to say. 

So, um, I guess the restlessness and the rushing does cause some actual problems with my freelance stuff and group work, not just social embarrassment. I'm so sorry if I wasn't clear about that before! Does that make more sense now? I hope I'm giving you the right information.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports childhood-onset (elementary school) symptoms of inattention (losing track of directions, rushing work, needing parental supervision to complete homework) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (fidgeting, needing to move, blurting out answers, interrupting during group work). These symptoms have persisted into adulthood and now cause functional impairment across multiple domains: academic (missed lecture content, extended homework time, stressed grades), occupational/freelance (lost contracts, missed competition), and social (friends/classmates hesitant to collaborate due to impulsivity and rushed follow-through). Both inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptom clusters are present with cross-situational impairment, meeting criteria for combined presentation ADHD.
